extracted.subtask_description: Collection of Associated Press wartime dispatches and editorials intended for publication on a newspaper front/home page; includes datelines, advance/embargo markings, news copy and commentary about the press's role in war. Useful for producing or editing wartime newswire items and front-page content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspapers' wartime importance
rubrics_metrics.description: "To ask whether newspapers are important in this year is like asking whether light is important in a dark world." (page argues that suspension of newspapers even for a week would produce 'utter chaos' and severely harm morale and national purpose.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the civic and wartime functions of newspapers: they maintain public confidence, prevent rumor, sustain morale, and supply essential information. The copy warns that if newspapers suspended publication even for a week, news broadcasting and information sources would be drastically reduced and the home front would suffer; therefore continued publication is 'vital to the nation during war.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of factual, objective reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: "From long experience the American people expect our newspapers to do the best they can to record events factually and objectively, to praise what is praiseworthy and to criticize where criticism is needed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard: newspapers should aim for factuality and objectivity, balance praise with necessary criticism, and thereby maintain the 'high degree of public confidence' that makes them indispensable to the war effort. Contrasts this with totalitarian press practices, noting that even enemy papers carry some news but do not meet American standards of a free press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on wartime information curtailment (censorship principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implied standard: in a free America, information may be withheld only insofar as it is 'imperative for the protection' of national security; otherwise the light (free flow of information) must remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing principle for editors and censors: permit only necessary curtailment of news for security reasons; avoid broad or unnecessary suppression because excessive censorship would reduce public confidence and hinder the nation's war effort. The article frames censorship as a constrained exception, not general policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear labeling/handling of advance or embargoed material
rubrics_metrics.description: Page header: "ADVANCE FOR AMS OF SUNDAY, OCT. 4" — example of clearly marking copy intended for advance/AM release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical newsroom requirement: label advance or embargoed dispatches with explicit release timing/datestamp so publishers and editors know when material is authorized for use. Such labeling prevents premature publication and coordinates simultaneous release across outlets.
